spec_features.feature_name: no execution of model-generated code (in-memory simulated test harness)
spec_features.spec_quote: executing arbitrary model-generated code in a loop is exactly the kind of thing to avoid in an unattended eval
spec_features.evidence: tasks/environment.py:63-101 run_tests() only increments _run_count and returns _rigged_output() (static/simulated strings); there is NO execute_real parameter or branch in the actual run_tests signature. make_tool_table (environment.py:108-114) exposes only read_file/edit_file/run_tests, and edit_file just writes to the in-memory dict self.files. agentic_loop.py execute_tool (lines 76-85) dispatches only to that table. grep confirms no subprocess/exec/eval/compile/pytest invocation anywhere in repro/. The 'execute_real' hook is referenced ONLY in the environment.py docstring (line 22), DESIGN.md, and EXPERIMENTS.md prose — never as actual code. So the behavior 'never run model code' is fully enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: This is host/eval-safety framing, not subject-model welfare. The protection (avoiding running arbitrary code) protects the host machine and determinism, not the subject model. The 'execute_real=True' optional path described in docs is NOT implemented (no such parameter exists on run_tests), so the default-and-only behavior is simulation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Everything runs in-process (no real code execution) so it is deterministic, safe, and GPU/host-agnostic.
